$comment: Plugins the HOSTED Forge serves, beyond the ones bundled in plugins/.
The hosted instance cannot install plugins through its own UI: that route is
code execution in the Forge process and is refused outright under
UWP_PUBLIC_READONLY=1. So the plugin set is deployed, not clicked -- which
also means it is reviewable, versioned, and identical after every deploy
instead of drifting with whatever someone once installed by hand.
Versions are pinned, never 'latest'. The hosted free tier is what visitors
judge the product by; it should change when someone decides it changes.
Source is the GitHub repo, the same one Forge's own installer accepts and
the same one the plugin's updateSource names -- so the hosted instance runs
what a user installing it themselves would get, not a different build.
NOT npm: @unleashwp/lumo is the MCP server distribution and its `files`
field omits plugin.json and server.mjs, so the tarball is not a Forge
plugin at all. Verified by unpacking 0.4.1.
unleash-wp/lumo is private today, which also means no user can install Lumo
as its own manifest advertises. Making it public fixes both at once; until
then the deploy needs HOSTED_PLUGINS_TOKEN with read access.

plugins.why: Lumo Free: curated, source-verified WordPress entries from a bundled snapshot. The free tier of the paid knowledge base, and the reason a visitor has a reason to come back.
